where: ch21.2 second paragraph (Stunting ... too little high-quality protein at very low cost in poor upland districts)
current: "Vietnam has two protein problems ... too much meat in cities, and too little high-quality protein at very low cost in poor upland districts."
proposed: Keep the under-five statement and add: "In upland boarding schools the plate is not the gap. In 13 ethnic-minority boarding schools in five provinces that publish menus (22 school-weeks, 2026), 240 of 242 lunches and dinners carried a meat, fish or egg dish and pork led 74% of them; four kitchens that publish cost sheets bought 107 to 215 g of raw pork per pupil a day. Kitchen-weighed boarding diets in Yen Bai (2019) met protein and zinc needs (zinc 131 to 157%) but supplied 36.5% of calcium and 41 to 45% of vitamin A. The low-cost protein problem sits before school age, at breakfast (86% of boarding breakfasts carry little or no animal food) and in home diets, which this evidence does not measure."
evidence_source_ids: UPL-01 to UPL-17; UPL-18; UPL-19; APR-27
